summary.business_type: Local Service / Tourist Attraction (Independent Travel Guide)
top_findings: No robots.txt file — search engines have no crawl guidance
Zero structured data / JSON-LD on all 11 pages — misses rich result opportunities for TouristAttraction, FAQ, and Article schemas
Duplicate brand name in all page titles due to BaseLayout suffix pattern
Missing canonical tags on all pages — no self-canonical or cross-domain directives
Blog page has zero real content — four dead links to '#' with no actual blog posts
About page is dangerously thin (~150 words) — harms E-E-A-T signals
No og:image on any page — social sharing has no preview images
Images lack explicit width/height attributes — CLS risk on every page
Four unused font subsets shipped (cyrillic, cyrillic-ext, latin-ext, vietnamese) adding ~46 KB unnecessary payload for English-only site
No llms.txt, no author/bio signals, no content freshness dates — weak AI search readiness
quick_wins: Add robots.txt to public/ directory (2 minutes)
Add canonical self-referencing tags to BaseLayout (1 line change)
Remove redundant brand-name suffix from titles, or make BaseLayout smarter about deduplication
Add og:image meta to BaseLayout using the hero image
Add width/height attributes to all tags for CLS prevention
Add JSON-LD TouristAttraction schema to homepage and key landing pages
Add JSON-LD FAQPage schema to /faq/ and /volunteer-program/
Drop unused font subsets — subset Geist Variable to Latin only via @fontsource config
Create llms.txt at site root with page summaries

categories.name: Technical SEO
what_works: Sitemap auto-generated via @astrojs/sitemap — valid XML, 11 URLs indexed
Clean, minified static HTML — zero JavaScript framework overhead
Proper lang="en" declaration
Semantic HTML5 with logical heading structure
Favicon as lightweight SVG
All internal links use clean absolute paths (/volunteer-program/, etc.)

findings.title: No robots.txt file
findings.description: Neither dist/ nor public/ contains a robots.txt. Search engines have no crawl directives — no sitemap reference, no disallow rules. This is a basic missing file that every site needs.
findings.recommendation: Create public/robots.txt with sitemap pointer: `Sitemap: https://dujiangyanpanda.com/sitemap-index.xml`

findings.title: Missing canonical tags on all pages
findings.description: No <link rel="canonical"> on any of the 11 pages. Without self-referencing canonicals, search engines may treat URL variants (trailing slash, www, HTTP/HTTPS) as duplicates.
findings.recommendation: Add self-referencing canonical in BaseLayout using Astro.url. Also add a <meta name="robots" content="index, follow"> directive.

findings.title: Sitemap lacks lastmod, changefreq, and priority
findings.description: sitemap-0.xml contains bare <url><loc> entries with no metadata. While Google says it ignores priority/changefreq, lastmod is a strong crawl signal and should always be included.
findings.recommendation: Configure @astrojs/sitemap to include lastmod. Add a custom sitemap config in astro.config.mjs.

findings.title: No hreflang or language targeting
findings.description: The site is English-only but doesn't declare a self-referencing hreflang. Important for international travel audiences.
findings.recommendation: Add <link rel="alternate" hreflang="en" href="..."> self-reference to BaseLayout.

findings.title: No 404 page
findings.description: No custom 404 page exists. Missing pages return whatever the hosting platform serves — usually an unhelpful default.
findings.recommendation: Create src/pages/404.astro with navigation back to homepage and key pages.

findings.title: No RSS feed for blog
findings.description: Blog page exists but has no RSS/Atom feed. This limits discoverability and syndication options.
findings.recommendation: Add @astrojs/rss integration once blog posts are created.

categories.name: Content Quality
what_works: Well-written, natural English across all informational pages
Detailed practical content: specific prices, schedules, seasonal data
Genuinely useful for international travelers planning a visit
Strong topical depth on volunteer, tickets, and transit pages
Good FAQ content (8 questions on FAQ page, 5 on volunteer page, 5 on homepage)
Transparent disclaimer in footer about non-affiliation

findings.title: Blog page has no real content — all posts are dead links
findings.description: The /blog/ page lists 4 blog post titles with dates (March-June 2026) but all links go to '#'. Google will see this as a soft 404 or thin content page. It actively harms the site's quality signals.
findings.recommendation: Either create real blog posts immediately or remove the blog listing page. Do not publish placeholder pages with dead links.

findings.title: About page is dangerously thin
findings.description: The /about/ page contains ~150 words across 3 generic paragraphs. No author bios, no credentials, no contact info, no team info. This is a major E-E-A-T weakness, especially for a site providing travel advice.
findings.recommendation: Expand to 500+ words. Add author/team information with credentials, contact methods, editorial policy, and content update frequency.

findings.title: No author or content attribution anywhere
findings.description: No page has author bylines, bio information, or any indicator of who wrote the content. For a travel guide site, Google's E-E-A-T guidelines heavily weight demonstrable expertise and author transparency.
findings.recommendation: Add author schema and bylines. Even a collective 'Editorial Team' attribution is better than nothing.

findings.title: No content freshness signals
findings.description: No 'last updated' dates, publish dates, or any temporal signals on any informational page. Travel information (prices, schedules, policies) changes frequently and Google values freshness indicators.
findings.recommendation: Add 'Last updated' dates to key pages (tickets, volunteer-program, how-to-get-there, visit-guide). The footer already shows © 2026 — use that as a minimum baseline.

findings.title: No contact page or contact information
findings.description: The about page mentions 'reach out through our contact channels' but no contact page exists. Missing contact info hurts both user trust and E-E-A-T.
findings.recommendation: Create a /contact/ page with at minimum an email address or contact form.

findings.title: Missing privacy policy and terms pages
findings.description: No privacy policy or terms of use pages. Even if not collecting user data, these are trust signals and increasingly expected by Google.
findings.recommendation: Add /privacy/ and /terms/ pages as part of the footer.

categories.name: On-Page SEO
what_works: Every page has a unique, keyword-rich title tag
Every page has a unique meta description of appropriate length (140-165 chars)
H1 on every page is clear and descriptive
Consistent header/footer navigation with key pages
Good internal linking — cross-references between related pages (e.g., volunteer page links to tickets)
Proper OpenGraph title and description on all pages

findings.title: Duplicate brand name in all titles due to BaseLayout suffix
findings.description: BaseLayout appends '| Dujiangyan Panda Base' to every title. Pages that already include the brand name become redundant. Examples: Homepage becomes 'Dujiangyan Panda Base - Volunteer, Tickets & Visit Guide 2026 | Dujiangyan Panda Base'; About becomes 'About - Dujiangyan Panda Base Guide | Dujiangyan Panda Base'. This wastes valuable title tag real estate and looks unprofessional in SERPs.
findings.recommendation: Either remove the brand suffix from BaseLayout and let each page own its full title, or make the suffix conditional (don't append if the page title already contains 'Dujiangyan').

findings.title: Homepage title includes year '2026' — will become outdated
findings.description: The homepage title tag includes '2026'. This hardcoded year will age poorly and requires manual updates annually.
findings.recommendation: Remove the year from the title, or use a dynamic year via the Astro template (already done in footer).

findings.title: Blog page uses <h2> for page heading instead of <h1>
findings.description:
The /blog/ page uses

as the main page heading. The eyebrow 'Blog' is styled as a

findings.recommendation:
Change to

findings.title: FAQ page uses <h2> tags inside <details> elements — non-standard and inaccessible
findings.description: The FAQ questions are marked up as <h2> inside <details><summary>. This is invalid HTML (interactive content inside interactive content) and may confuse assistive technologies.
findings.recommendation: Remove <h2> wrapping from FAQ headings inside <details>. Use <summary> alone with appropriate styling.

findings.title: Missing Twitter/X card metadata
findings.description: No twitter:card, twitter:title, or twitter:description meta tags on any page.
findings.recommendation: Add Twitter card metadata to BaseLayout (at minimum twitter:card = summary_large_image).

categories.name: Schema / Structured Data
what_works: No structured data currently implemented — clean baseline to build from

findings.title: Zero structured data on the entire site
findings.description: Not a single JSON-LD block or microdata attribute exists across all 11 pages. This is the single largest missed opportunity: the site has TouristAttraction content, FAQ content, article listings, and organizational information — all of which could qualify for rich results in Google SERPs.
findings.recommendation: Implement these schemas in priority order: (1) Organization + WebSite (site-wide), (2) TouristAttraction on homepage and attraction pages, (3) FAQPage on /faq/ and /volunteer-program/, (4) Article on blog posts, (5) BreadcrumbList on all pages, (6) LocalBusiness if representing an actual tour operator.

categories.name: Performance (CWV)
what_works: Static HTML site — server response time will be fast on any CDN
CSS bundled into single 26.7 KB file
All images are WebP format
No client-side JavaScript framework or heavy JS bundles
No third-party scripts (no analytics, no ads, no tracking)
Proper lazy loading on non-hero images
Hero image uses loading="eager"

findings.title: No explicit image dimensions — CLS risk
findings.description: Every tag lacks explicit width and height attributes. The hero image and content images will push page layout as they load, causing Cumulative Layout Shift. This directly impacts the CLS metric in Core Web Vitals.
findings.recommendation: Add width and height attributes to all tags. For responsive images, include these alongside CSS `height: auto` and `max-width: 100%`.

findings.title: Unused font subsets shipped unnecessarily
findings.description: Five Geist Variable woff2 files totaling ~75 KB are loaded. Only the Latin subset (28.7 KB) is needed for English content. Cyrillic (14.7 KB), Latin-ext (16.1 KB), Cyrillic-ext (7.2 KB), and Vietnamese (7.8 KB) add ~46 KB of unnecessary download.
findings.recommendation: Configure @fontsource-variable/geist to load only the Latin subset. If using Tailwind's font import, restrict to the needed unicode-range in the CSS.

findings.title: No responsive images (srcset/sizes)
findings.description: All images use single-source URLs. The hero image at 178 KB loads at full resolution on mobile devices where a smaller version would suffice.
findings.recommendation: Use Astro's Image component or sharp to generate responsive srcset variants. This is particularly important for the 178 KB hero image.

findings.title: No font-display strategy visible
findings.description: Font loading behavior is not explicitly controlled. Without font-display: swap, text may be invisible during font load (FOIT).
findings.recommendation: Ensure @fontsource CSS includes font-display: swap. Alternatively, set it explicitly in global.css.

categories.name: Images
what_works: All 5 images are WebP — optimal format for web
Good descriptive alt text on every image
Reasonable file sizes (22-178 KB range)
Hero image loaded eagerly; content images lazy-loaded
Images have aspect-ratio preserved via CSS (aspect-[4/5], aspect-[2/1], aspect-[4/3])

findings.title: No explicit width/height attributes on images
findings.description: Same CLS issue noted in Performance. All tags need explicit dimensions.
findings.recommendation: Add width/height to all tags. Use CSS aspect-ratio as a complement, not a replacement.

findings.title: Hero image at 178 KB is the largest asset
findings.description: The hero-panda-bamboo.webp at 178 KB is reasonable for a full-bleed hero but could be compressed further. No smaller variant for mobile exists.
findings.recommendation: Compress to 120-140 KB range or generate a mobile variant at 80-100 KB via srcset.

findings.title: No og:image on any page
findings.description: Social sharing previews will show no image. For a visually-driven travel site, this is a significant missed engagement opportunity.
findings.recommendation: Set a default og:image in BaseLayout (use hero-panda-bamboo.webp or create a dedicated 1200x630 social card).

categories.name: AI Search Readiness
what_works: Clean semantic HTML — easy for AI crawlers to parse
Well-structured content with clear headings and sections
English-language content targeting international audience
Good content depth on key informational pages
No JavaScript-rendered content — fully static, crawler-friendly

findings.title: No llms.txt file
findings.description: No /llms.txt exists at the site root. This file provides structured context to LLM crawlers and is becoming an expected signal for AI search readiness.
findings.recommendation: Create public/llms.txt with a brief site description and links to key pages. Follow the llms.txt spec format.

findings.title: No structured data — AI crawler comprehension gap
findings.description: Without JSON-LD, AI crawlers (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews) must infer page meaning from text alone. Schema provides explicit entity definitions that improve citation accuracy.
findings.recommendation: Adding TouristAttraction, FAQPage, and Organization schemas will directly improve how AI search engines understand and cite this site.

findings.title: No author/credential signals
findings.description: AI search engines prioritize content with clear provenance. No author information, credentials, or content methodology is present.
findings.recommendation: Add author pages, editorial guidelines, and content methodology statements.

findings.title: No robots.txt — may block AI crawlers inadvertently
findings.description: Without an explicit robots.txt, some AI crawlers (like GPTBot) have separate user-agent directives. It's better to explicitly allow or disallow them.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit GPTBot and anthropic-ai directives to robots.txt (allow or disallow, with a decision made).
